_comment: SPARK — S175 P2: THE ORC WARLORD'S DIREWOLF (owner R149). The clips were generated in S173;
this is the spec that finally turns them into a sheet.
⛔ WHAT THIS REPLACES. `direwolf` has been in GOBLIN_KINDS since S168 and in the ATLASES table
since S173 B5 — pointed at '/godly/goblin-hound/anim/goblin-hound'. It has been BORROWING the
goblin hound's sheet, which is why the owner kept seeing a hound where his wolf should be. The
art existed the whole time; nothing had ever been packed from it.
⭐ GEOMETRY IS COPIED FROM THE HOUND ON PURPOSE, not chosen. cellH 200 and the idle-7 / walk-3 /
attack-5 cadence are exactly the stand-in's shipped values, so re-pointing the renderer changes
WHICH animal is drawn and nothing else — no size jump, no cadence change, nothing else to review.
⚠ enclosedWhiteLimitPct is the TUNED 4e-05, set explicitly. The 0.003 default is 75x looser and
taking it by omission is the S165 defect the owner reported as "some of them have that white
background because not cut out too well". A quadruped is the worst case for it — four legs make
several enclosed background pockets a single-blob matte will happily keep.
⭐ NO sampleStart ON ANY PLAYABLE ROW, AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. idle is pillarboxed in
all 24 sampled frames, which is the stable case the content-column crop already handles. walk is
a clean PASS today — ART_VEO_PROTOCOL.md's S173 verdict table condemns it, but walk.mp4 was
RE-ROLLED at 21:17 after that table was written and the table was never updated. attack passed
when it was written and passes now.
⛔ DIE IS A STILL, AND IT IS THE OWNER'S RULING, NOT A SHORTCUT. His words: "I already have a
purpose drawn like dead wolf, so we should use that." The alternative on the table was
sampleStart:68 on die.mp4, which packs cleanly and is ARTISTICALLY EMPTY — the collapse happens
at frames 20-32 inside the pillarboxed region, and frames 68-95 are a motionless corpse with an
identical bbox. Twelve frames of a dead-still body, for a row the renderer holds on anyway.
The drawn corpse is the same static property and a far better picture, for the same $0.
⚠ THE STILL FORCED A PACKER FIX, recorded here because a future session will hit it again:
normaliseStateScale measures `die` at FRAME 0 precisely because, in a CLIP, frame 0 is the
creature still STANDING and therefore pose-comparable with idle. A still has no standing frame —
the still IS the corpse — so the pass read a legitimately short subject as zoom error and would
have inflated the dead wolf ~1.7x to stand as tall as the living one. `still`-sourced states are
now exempt (build-sprite-atlas.mjs, the normaliseStateScale block).
⛔ COST OF THIS FILE: $0.00. Every input already existed on disk.
